records.source: שִׁ֥יר מִזְמ֗וֹר לִבְנֵ֫י קֹ֥רַח לַמְנַצֵּ֣חַ עַל־מָחֲלַ֣ת לְעַנּ֑וֹת מַ֝שְׂכִּ֗יל לְהֵימָ֥ן הָאֶזְרָחִֽי׃
records.gloss: A song, a psalm of [the] sons of Korah, for the director, on mahalath leannoth, a maskil of Heman the Ezrahite.
pieces: A song. A psalm of the sons of Korah. For the music director. On mahalath leannoth. A maskil of Heman the Ezrahite.

L.1: A song; a psalm of the sons of Korah. For the director: on mahalath leannoth. A maskil of Heman the Ezrahite.

R.1: A song with music, from the family of Korah. For the leader of the music. To a tune for times of suffering. A song to teach, by Heman the Ezrahite.

decisions.choice: The title is verse 1
decisions.reason: The title is part of the Hebrew text and is counted as verse 1, so the verse numbers here are one higher than in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: the sons of Korah: a family of Levite singers
decisions.reason: The descendants of Korah, a Levite (Numbers 26:11), served as gatekeepers and singers at the temple (1 Chronicles 9:19; 2 Chronicles 20:19). Eleven psalms carry their name (42-49, 84-85, 87-88). "Of" may mean the psalm belongs to their collection or was written by one of them.

decisions.choice: the director: the one who leads the music
decisions.reason: As in 4:1, probably the leader of the temple music.

decisions.choice: mahalath leannoth: probably a tune or manner of singing
decisions.reason: Mahalath (also in the title of 53:1) may come from the word for sickness; leannoth may mean "to afflict" or "to sing". The words may name a tune or say how the psalm was sung. Their exact sense is no longer known.

decisions.choice: maskil: a song of insight, or a skillful song
decisions.reason: The word comes from the verb "to have insight, act wisely". As a heading for thirteen psalms it may mark a song that teaches, or one composed with skill; its exact sense is no longer known.

decisions.choice: Heman the Ezrahite
decisions.reason: Heman was a famous wise man (1 Kings 5) and is listed among the sons of Zerah of Judah (1 Chronicles 2:6); "Ezrahite" probably means of the family of Zerah. A Heman was also one of David's chief singers (1 Chronicles 15:19). The title names both the sons of Korah and Heman, perhaps two notes about the psalm's origin.

decisions.choice: to a tune for times of suffering; a song to teach
decisions.reason: Readable gives the likeliest sense of the terms (m4, m5).

records.heading: A prayer from the darkness

records.source: יְ֭הוָה אֱלֹהֵ֣י יְשׁוּעָתִ֑י יוֹם־צָעַ֖קְתִּי בַלַּ֣יְלָה נֶגְדֶּֽךָ׃
records.gloss: YHWH, God of my salvation, [by] day I have cried out, in the night before you.
pieces: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, God who saves me, \q I have cried for help by day, and at night I am before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

L.2: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, God of my salvation, \q [by] day I have cried out, in the night [I am] before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

R.2: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, my God, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are the one who saves me. \q I call to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} for help all day, and I keep calling at night.

decisions.choice: God of my salvation: the one hope in the psalm
decisions.reason: Psalm 88 has no turn to praise and ends in darkness. Its one hope is that the psalmist still calls the LORD "God of my salvation" and keeps praying to him (verses 10, 14).

decisions.choice: by day I cried, at night before you
alternatives: by day I cry out, and by night, before you
decisions.reason: The two halves of the line are day and night: he cries to God all the time. The second half has no verb; "I am" (or "I cry") is understood.

decisions.choice: [I am]
decisions.reason: Literal brackets the verb the second half implies (m2).

records.gloss: May my prayer come before you; incline your ear to my cry.
pieces: Let my prayer make its way into {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} presence; \q bend down and hear me as I cry.

L.3: Let my prayer come before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; \q incline {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} ear to my cry.

R.3: Please hear my prayer. \q Listen when I cry out to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: my cry: a loud, ringing cry
decisions.reason: The word (rinnah) is often a ringing shout of joy (30:6); here it is a loud cry for help (17:1).

decisions.choice: incline your ear: listen closely
decisions.reason: As in 86:1.

records.source: כִּֽי־שָֽׂבְעָ֣ה בְרָע֣וֹת נַפְשִׁ֑י וְחַיַּ֗י לִשְׁא֥וֹל הִגִּֽיעוּ׃
records.gloss: For full with troubles [is] my soul, and my life to Sheol has drawn near.
pieces: For I have had my fill of troubles, \q and my life has come to the edge of Sheol.

L.4: For my soul is full of troubles, \q and my life has drawn near to Sheol.

R.4: My life is filled to the top with trouble. \q I am close to the place of the dead.

decisions.choice: full: had one's fill
decisions.reason: The verb (sava') is used for eating one's fill. Here it is a bitter picture: he has been fed on trouble until he can take no more.

decisions.choice: Sheol: the place of the dead
decisions.reason: As in 6:6.

decisions.choice: I (B); my life (R)
decisions.reason: Nefesh is the whole living self; Literal keeps "soul".

records.source: נֶ֭חְשַׁבְתִּי עִם־י֣וֹרְדֵי ב֑וֹר הָ֝יִ֗יתִי כְּגֶ֣בֶר אֵֽין־אֱיָֽל׃
records.gloss: I am counted with those going down [to the] pit; I have become like a man without strength.
pieces: I am reckoned with those who descend into the pit; \q I have become like someone with no strength left.

L.5: I am counted with those who go down [to the] pit; \q I have become like {{gender:someone|a man}} [who has] no strength.

R.5: People think of me as already dead and buried. \q I have no strength left.

decisions.choice: the pit: the grave, the way down to Sheol
decisions.reason: The pit (bor) is a cistern or a grave; "those who go down to the pit" are the dying (28:1; 30:4).

decisions.choice: a man without strength
decisions.reason: The word for man (gever) suggests a strong man. He is a man in name, but the strength is gone.

decisions.choice: people think of me as already dead and buried
alternatives: I am counted with those who go down to the pit
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture means (m1).

records.source: בַּמֵּתִ֗ים חָ֫פְשִׁ֥י כְּמ֤וֹ חֲלָלִ֨ים׀שֹׁ֥כְבֵי קֶ֗בֶר אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹ֣א זְכַרְתָּ֣ם ע֑וֹד וְ֝הֵ֗מָּה מִיָּדְךָ֥ נִגְזָֽרוּ׃
records.gloss: Among the dead free, like [the] slain lying [in the] grave, whom not you remember anymore, and they from your hand are cut off.
pieces: I am turned loose among the dead, \q like those killed in battle who lie buried, whom {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} no longer keep in mind, \q who are beyond the reach of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand.

L.6: Among the dead [I am] set free, \q like [the] slain who lie [in the] grave, whom {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} remember no more, \q and they are cut off from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand.

R.6: I have been left among the dead, \q like people killed in battle and buried. \q You do not remember them anymore. They are cut off from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} help.

decisions.choice: free: cut loose, left to oneself
decisions.reason: The word (chofshi) is used for a slave set free (Exodus 21:2). Among the dead it is a bitter freedom: released from life and from God's care.

decisions.choice: cut off from your hand: beyond your help
decisions.reason: God's hand is his power to act and save. The dead, as the psalmist sees them, are out of its reach and out of his mind.

decisions.choice: the slain: those killed in battle
decisions.reason: The word (chalal) is used for the fallen in war, left in a common grave (Ezekiel 32:20-32).

records.gloss: You have put me in [the] pit of [the] lowest [places], in dark places, in [the] depths.
pieces: You have laid me at the bottom of the pit, \q in places of darkness, in the deep waters.

L.7: You have put me in the lowest pit, \q in dark places, in the depths.

R.7: You have put me at the very bottom of the pit, \q in the dark, deep down.

decisions.choice: you have put me: God is the one who has done it
decisions.reason: The psalmist does not blame his enemies or chance. Again and again he says that God has done this to him (verses 7-9, 17-19). The psalm leaves the complaint standing.

decisions.choice: the depths: the deep places of the sea
decisions.reason: The word (metsolot) is used of the sea's depths (Exodus 15:5; 69:3). The grave and the deep waters are both pictures of death.

records.source: עָ֭לַי סָמְכָ֣ה חֲמָתֶ֑ךָ וְכָל־מִ֝שְׁבָּרֶ֗יךָ עִנִּ֥יתָ סֶּֽלָה׃
records.gloss: On me has lain your wrath, and [with] all your breakers you have afflicted [me]. Selah.
pieces: Your fury presses down on me; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have crushed me under all {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} waves. Selah

L.8: Upon me {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} wrath has lain heavy, \q and with all {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} breakers {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have afflicted [me]. Selah

R.8: Your anger lies heavy on me. \q You have sent wave after wave crashing over me. Selah

decisions.choice: has lain: rests its weight on me
decisions.reason: The verb (samakh) means to lean or press on something; God's anger rests its full weight on him.

decisions.choice: your breakers: the waves that break over a drowning man
decisions.reason: The same picture is in 42:8 ("all your breakers and your waves have passed over me") and in Jonah's prayer from the deep (Jonah 2).

decisions.choice: Selah: a word whose meaning is no longer known
alternatives: lift up (the voice or the music)
decisions.reason: Selah stands at the end of a line 71 times in the Psalms and 3 times in Habakkuk 3. It is probably a direction for singing or music, perhaps a pause or an interlude; the ancient Greek translation renders it with a word meaning "interlude". It is not part of what is said, and here it marks a break after the line.

decisions.choice: Selah, kept as it is
decisions.reason: Its meaning is unknown (see the meaning decision on Selah), so every level keeps the word rather than guess, and keeps it apart from the sentence.

records.source: הִרְחַ֥קְתָּ מְיֻדָּעַ֗י מִ֫מֶּ֥נִּי שַׁתַּ֣נִי תוֹעֵב֣וֹת לָ֑מוֹ כָּ֝לֻ֗א וְלֹ֣א אֵצֵֽא׃
records.gloss: You have put far my acquaintances from me; you have made me abominations to them; shut in, and not I go out.
pieces: You have driven my friends away from me \q and made me loathsome to them; \q I am shut in, with no way out.

L.9: You have removed my acquaintances far from me; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have made me an abomination to them; \q [I am] shut in, and I cannot go out.

R.9: You have made my friends stay away from me. \q They find me disgusting. \q I am trapped like a prisoner, and I cannot get out.

decisions.choice: abominations: something people recoil from
decisions.reason: The word (to'evah) is what is detestable or repulsive. His friends now turn away from him in horror.

decisions.choice: shut in: confined like a prisoner or one set apart
decisions.reason: He may be shut up by sickness, as someone with a skin disease had to live apart (Leviticus 13:46), or he speaks of being trapped as in a prison. The picture is of complete isolation.

decisions.choice: like a prisoner
decisions.reason: Readable makes the picture of being shut in a comparison (m2).

records.source: עֵינִ֥י דָאֲבָ֗ה מִנִּ֫י עֹ֥נִי קְרָאתִ֣יךָ יְהוָ֣ה בְּכָל־י֑וֹם שִׁטַּ֖חְתִּי אֵלֶ֣יךָ כַפָּֽי׃
records.gloss: My eye has grown faint from affliction; I have called you, YHWH, every day; I have spread out to you my palms.
pieces: My eyes are worn out with misery. \q Day after day I call on {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, \q holding out my hands to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

L.10: My eye has grown faint from affliction; \q I have called [to] {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, every day; \q I have spread out my palms to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

R.10: I have cried so much that I can hardly see. \q {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, I call to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} every day. \q I lift my hands to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} in prayer.

decisions.choice: my eye has grown faint: worn out by grief
decisions.reason: Weeping and suffering dim the eyes (6:8; 31:10).

decisions.choice: spread out my palms: the gesture of prayer
decisions.reason: People prayed with open hands stretched out toward God (Exodus 9:29; 143:6).

decisions.choice: I have cried so much that I can hardly see
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture (m1).

records.gloss: For the dead will you do wonder[s]? Or shades — will they arise, will they praise you? Selah.
pieces: Are {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} wonders done for the dead? \q Do the spirits of the dead stand up to give {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} thanks? Selah

L.11: Will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do wonders for the dead? \q Or will [the] shades arise [and] praise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}? Selah

R.11: Will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do amazing things for dead people? \q Will the dead get up and thank {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}? Selah

decisions.choice: questions that expect the answer no
decisions.reason: Verses 11-13 are questions with an obvious answer: no. If the psalmist dies, God loses one who praises him (6:6; 30:10). The argument is a plea to act now.

decisions.choice: shades: the dead as weak shadows
decisions.reason: The word (repha'im) names the dead in Sheol as faint and powerless (Isaiah 14:9; 26:14).

decisions.choice: the psalm speaks from inside the darkness
decisions.reason: Here the dead do not rise to praise. Other Scripture holds out hope of rising from the dead (Isaiah 26:19; Daniel 12:2), but this psalm gives its questions no answer, and the translation leaves them as they are.

decisions.choice: Selah: a word whose meaning is no longer known
alternatives: lift up (the voice or the music)
decisions.reason: Selah stands at the end of a line 71 times in the Psalms and 3 times in Habakkuk 3. It is probably a direction for singing or music, perhaps a pause or an interlude; the ancient Greek translation renders it with a word meaning "interlude". It is not part of what is said, and here it marks a break after the line.

decisions.choice: Selah, kept as it is
decisions.reason: Its meaning is unknown (see the meaning decision on Selah), so every level keeps the word rather than guess, and keeps it apart from the sentence.

records.gloss: Will your loyal love be recounted in the grave, your faithfulness in Abaddon?
pieces: Does anyone tell of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} loyal love in the grave, \q or of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithfulness in Abaddon?

L.12: Will {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} loyal love be recounted in the grave, \q {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithfulness in Abaddon?

R.12: Does anyone in the grave talk about {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithful love? \q Can anyone in the place of destruction tell how loyal {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are?

decisions.choice: Abaddon: the place of destruction, a name for the realm of the dead
decisions.reason: The word means "destruction" and stands beside Sheol and death (Job 26:6; 28:22; Proverbs 15:11). In Revelation 9:11 it is the name of the angel of the abyss.

decisions.choice: loyal love
decisions.reason: As in 86:5 (chesed).

decisions.choice: the place of destruction
decisions.reason: Readable says what the name means (m1).

records.source: הֲיִוָּדַ֣ע בַּחֹ֣שֶׁךְ פִּלְאֶ֑ךָ וְ֝צִדְקָתְךָ֗ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ נְשִׁיָּֽה׃
records.gloss: Will your wonder be known in the darkness, and your righteousness in [the] land of forgetting?
pieces: Will anyone in the darkness know {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} wonders, \q or {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} saving justice in the land where all is forgotten?

L.13: Will {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} wonder[s] be known in the darkness, \q and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} righteousness in the land of forgetfulness?

R.13: Can people in the dark know about the amazing things {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do? \q Can people in the land of the forgotten know how {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} make things right?

decisions.choice: the land of forgetting: where the dead are forgotten
decisions.reason: The realm of the dead is where people are forgotten (31:13) and where nothing is remembered.

decisions.choice: righteousness: God's faithful, saving justice
decisions.reason: God's righteousness (tsedaqah) is his doing right by his people, shown in rescue (71:15).

decisions.choice: saving justice (B); how you make things right (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable bring out the sense of the word here (m2).

records.source: וַאֲנִ֤י׀אֵלֶ֣יךָ יְהוָ֣ה שִׁוַּ֑עְתִּי וּ֝בַבֹּ֗קֶר תְּֽפִלָּתִ֥י תְקַדְּמֶֽךָּ׃
records.gloss: But I, to you, YHWH, cry for help, and in the morning my prayer comes to meet you.
pieces: As for me, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, I keep calling to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} for help; \q at dawn my prayer is there to meet {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

L.14: But I, to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, cry for help, \q and in the morning my prayer comes to meet {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

R.14: But {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, I keep crying out to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} for help. \q When morning comes, I am already praying to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: but I: unlike the silent dead
decisions.reason: The dead cannot praise (verses 11-13), but he is still alive and still praying.

decisions.choice: comes to meet you: is there first
decisions.reason: The verb (qiddem) means to go out ahead to meet someone. His prayer is waiting for God at first light (5:4).

records.source: לָמָ֣ה יְ֭הוָה תִּזְנַ֣ח נַפְשִׁ֑י תַּסְתִּ֖יר פָּנֶ֣יךָ מִמֶּֽנִּי׃
records.gloss: Why, YHWH, do you reject my soul, [do] you hide your face from me?
pieces: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, why do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} cast me off? \q Why do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} turn {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} face away from me?

L.15: Why, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} reject my soul? \q [Why] do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} hide {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} face from me?

R.15: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, why have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} pushed me away? \q Why do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} turn away from me?

decisions.choice: reject: cast off, spurn
decisions.reason: The verb (zanach) is used for God casting off his people (44:10; 77:8).

decisions.choice: hide your face: withdraw your favor and presence
decisions.reason: God's face turned toward someone is his favor; to hide it is to leave him alone (13:2; 27:9).

decisions.choice: turn away from me
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture means (m2).

records.source: עָ֘נִ֤י אֲנִ֣י וְגֹוֵ֣עַ מִנֹּ֑עַר נָשָׂ֖אתִי אֵמֶ֣יךָ אָפֽוּנָה׃
records.gloss: Afflicted [am] I and dying from youth; I have borne your terrors; I am helpless.
pieces: From my youth I have been afflicted and close to dying; \q I bear {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} terrors and am at a loss.

L.16: Afflicted [am] I and dying from [my] youth; \q I have borne {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} terrors; I am in despair.

R.16: All my life I have suffered and been close to death. \q I have carried the terrors {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} send, and I do not know what to do.

decisions.choice: I am helpless: at a loss, without way out
decisions.reason: The word ('afunah) is found only here, and its sense is uncertain. It seems to describe someone overwhelmed and at the end of his strength.

decisions.choice: dying from youth: a lifelong affliction
decisions.reason: "From youth" suggests that his suffering has lasted most of his life.

records.gloss: Over me have passed your burning angers; your terrors have destroyed me.
pieces: Your blazing anger has rolled over me; \q {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} terrors have put an end to me.

L.17: Over me {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} burning angers have passed; \q {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} terrors have destroyed me.

R.17: Your anger has swept over me again and again. \q The terrible things {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do have destroyed me.

decisions.choice: burning angers: outbursts of fierce anger
decisions.reason: The word (charon) is anger that burns; the plural speaks of one outburst after another.

decisions.choice: destroyed me: silenced, put an end to
decisions.reason: The verb (tsamat) means to bring to an end or silence; this strengthened form is rare.

records.source: סַבּ֣וּנִי כַ֭מַּיִם כָּל־הַיּ֑וֹם הִקִּ֖יפוּ עָלַ֣י יָֽחַד׃
records.gloss: They have surrounded me like water all the day; they have closed in on me together.
pieces: Like water they swirl around me the whole day; \q from every side at once they close in.

L.18: They have surrounded me like water all the day; \q they have closed in on me altogether.

R.18: Like floodwaters, they are all around me all day long. \q They have closed in on me from every side.

decisions.choice: they: God's anger and terrors
decisions.reason: "They" are the burning angers and terrors of verse 17, pictured as flood waters.

decisions.choice: like water: the waters of death
decisions.reason: Rising water is a common picture of death closing in (18:5; 69:2-3).

records.source: הִרְחַ֣קְתָּ מִ֭מֶּנִּי אֹהֵ֣ב וָרֵ֑עַ מְֽיֻדָּעַ֥י מַחְשָֽׁךְ׃
records.gloss: You have put far from me one loving and a friend; my acquaintances [are] darkness.
pieces: You have taken far from me those I love and my friends; \q my one companion is the dark.

L.19: You have removed far from me [the one who] loves [me] and [my] companion; \q my acquaintances [are] darkness.

R.19: You have taken away the people I love and my friends. \q Now all I have for company is darkness.

decisions.choice: my acquaintances: darkness
decisions.reason: The last line has no verb. It probably means that darkness is now his only companion; it may also mean that the people he knew are lost to him in the dark. Either way the psalm ends on the word "darkness".

decisions.choice: a psalm that ends without relief
decisions.reason: Unlike nearly every other lament, Psalm 88 ends without any word of hope or praise. It stands in Scripture as a prayer for those whose darkness has not lifted. The translation does not soften its ending.

decisions.choice: friends driven away
decisions.reason: The line takes up verse 9 ("you have removed my acquaintances far from me").
